subject: Post-call recap: pricing, token sizing, and burst/overage options
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mejia <carlos@finlytics.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap: pricing, token sizing, and burst/overage options

Carlos — thanks for the time just now. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of what we heard
- Current baseline: ~120M tokens / month across ingestion + generation.
- Peak/spike pattern: expected feature launch that could drive ~6–8M tokens/day for short periods (2–7 days) during rollout.
- Target budget range you mentioned: $10k–$15k / month for the first 3 months of the pilot.

Pricing guardrails we discussed (initial proposal)
- Target list: aim for ~$120 / 1M tokens for on-demand usage (pilot pricing).
- Committed (reserved) option: we can offer a committed tier that brings unit cost down to ~$90 / 1M for the committed volume (min term 3 months).
- Overage / burst: for short spikes we recommend an elastic allowance + burst window. See options below.

Burst / overage options (we can pick one or combine)
1) Elastic allowance: 10% of monthly committed tokens usable without overage at monthly reconciliation.
2) Short-term burst window: Allow up to 2x daily quota for up to 72 hours. If exceeded, overage billed at $180 / 1M tokens (flat overage rate).
3) Reservation + burst: Purchase a modest committed pool (e.g., 50M/mo) at $90 / 1M, with an additional burst buffer priced at $120 / 1M for transient usage above the committed pool.

Action items / next steps
- Carlos: confirm the expected day-zero spike profile (dates and duration) so we can size a pilot commit.
- Ben / Karthik: I’ve attached our usage worksheet and a draft MAP — please review pricing lines and suggested SLA/overage language.
- Carlos: let me know if the $120 / 1M target is workable inside the $10k–$15k monthly range for month 1. If not, we’ll propose a commit/discount structure.

Attachments: FinLytics_usage_estimates.xlsx, FinLytics_mutual_action_plan.docx

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up tomorrow if helpful.

—
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Carlos Mejia <carlos@finlytics.co>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: pricing, token sizing, and burst/overage options

Kimberly — thanks for the clear write-up. Quick answers and a couple clarifying Qs: 

Numbers / constraints
- Baseline: correct, ~120M tokens / month today (mostly embedding + short generations).
- Launch spike: expecting ~6–8M/day for the first 5 business days of the launch, then taper to ~2–3M/day. Could be higher if adoption is stronger — we want headroom.
- Our internal budget (pilot): closer to the low end of what I said on the call — likely $10k / month for the first month unless we can secure a committed discount.

Clarifying questions
1) If we do the 2x daily quota for 72 hours path, how quickly can you increase the quota? We need near-immediate capacity for the launch window.
2) If we hit the overage rate ($180 / 1M), can we cap the absolute monthly spend or enable an automated alert + soft-stop?

What we need from Redwood to decide (by EOD Friday)
- A short comparison table: committed vs on-demand vs burst-overage (with unit costs and a worked example for our 5-day spike).
- Confirmation of API rate limits / per-tenant concurrency during bursts (we need to know if throttling will affect tail latency).

If you can share the worked numbers (using the attached usage sheet) and confirm the operational behavior we can make a call on whether to do a small commit.

–Carlos
Head of Platform Engineering
FinLytics
carlos@finlytics.co

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mejia <carlos@finlytics.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: pricing, token sizing, and burst/overage options

Carlos — thanks, super helpful. Quick answers and I’ll follow up with the worked example table by EOD Friday: 

1) Quota increases & burst activation
- We can route burst traffic automatically if you’re on a hosted plan; capacity is often available within minutes if we have an autoscale buffer. For Dedicated/Private we’ll need a short provisioning window (hours) depending on instance availability.
- Operationally: enable an "elastic burst" flag in the Console and we’ll route to a higher-capacity cluster for the duration of the window. For pilot, we can pre-warm capacity for your launch date if you provide the exact time window.

2) Spend protections
- Yes — we can configure an automated alert at a custom spend threshold and a soft-stop (reject calls) if you want an absolute cap. For pilots we typically enable alerts + a 24-hour soft-stop grace period before hard stops.

Worked example (summary preview) — I’ll attach a short table with exact numbers by EOD Friday. Example assumptions:
- If you run 6.5M tokens/day for 5 days (~32.5M tokens), then:
  • On-demand at $120 / 1M = $3,900 for the spike portion.
  • If committed at $90 / 1M for a 50M committed pool, the incremental above-commit billed at $120 / 1M.
  • If burst overage rate ($180 / 1M) applies to the exceeded tokens, that would be $5,850 for the same spike.

Next steps
- I’ll send a short committed vs on-demand vs burst table + an example cost calc (using the sheet you filled) by Friday.
- Please confirm launch date window so we can pre-warm.

Attached for your reference: pricing-options-summary.pdf (high-level plan sketches).

—
Kimberly

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: pricing, token sizing, and burst/overage options

Looping in our recommended commercial language and a practical playbook we can put in the MAP: 

Suggested commercial guardrails for pilot
- Elastic allowance: include 10% buffer of committed tokens monthly (no overage charge, reconciled monthly).
- Burst window: permit up to 2x daily run-rate for 72 hours without requiring immediate contract changes. Beyond that, overage billed at 1.5x list on-demand rate (we proposed $180 / 1M in the client-facing doc).
- Soft spend cap: include an API-level soft-stop we can set at the customer-requested threshold (FinLytics asked for $10k for month 1).

Operational asks for Sales/Ops
- Kimberly: confirm the exact UTC window for the launch so Ops can pre-warm.
- Karthik: can you review the attachment names and ensure the MAP includes legal-approved overage language?

I’ve attached a short internal playbook (pricing-options-summary.pdf) — keep it internal until legal signs off.

—Ben
Principal Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
